examples.prompt: A washer costs $800 with $100 down and 12 monthly payments of $64. Find amount financed, finance charge, and deferred payment price.
examples.title: A – Find the amounts
steps: Amount Financed = $800 – $100 = $700.
Total of Payments = 12 × $64 = $768. Finance Charge = $768 – $700 = $68.
Deferred Payment Price = $768 + $100 = $868.
The deferred payment price includes the down payment plus all future payments.
Those future payments include interest (finance charge) on top of the amount financed.
Thus the total paid over time exceeds the original cash price.

formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Amount Financed} = \text{Cash Price} - \text{Down Payment}$$ $$\text{Finance Charge} = \text{Total of Payments} - \text{Amount Financed}$$ $$\text{Deferred Payment Price} = \text{Total of Payments} + \text{Down Payment}$$
notes: Total of Payments = Monthly Payment × Number of Payments.
Finance charge includes interest plus any credit‑related fees.
formulaCard.title: Key Installment Formulas

explanation: [[kw:Amount financed]] is the amount actually borrowed: $$\text{Amount Financed} = \text{Cash Price} - \text{Down Payment}$$.
[[kw:Finance charge]] (total interest) is the cost of borrowing: $$\text{Finance Charge} = \text{Total of Payments} - \text{Amount Financed}$$.
[[kw:Deferred payment price]] is the total cost of the purchase on credit: $$\text{Deferred Payment Price} = \text{Total of Payments} + \text{Down Payment}$$.
This breakdown is required by the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z) so consumers understand the true cost.
[[imp:Always compare the deferred payment price to the cash price to see the real cost of credit.]]

discoveryHook.scenario: The truck ad showed a $194.38 monthly payment. We can verify this: ($2,617.80 + $9,045) ÷ 60 = $194.38. Alternatively, an amortization table (Table 14-2) gives the payment per $100 financed. For 60 months at 10.5% APR, the factor is $2.15 per $100, so payment = ($9,045 / 100) × $2.15 ≈ $194.47 (close to $194.38).

explanation: [[kw:Monthly payment]] is the amount paid each period to repay the loan plus interest.
By formula: $$\text{Monthly Payment} = \frac{\text{Finance Charge} + \text{Amount Financed}}{\text{Number of Payments}}$$.

By amortization table: 1. Find the table factor for the given APR and number of payments (per $100 financed). 2. Compute: $$\text{Payment} = \frac{\text{Amount Financed}}{100} \times \text{Table Factor}$$.
Both methods give approximately the same result; the amortization table is more precise for varying APRs.
[[imp:The monthly payment includes both principal and interest, with interest higher at the beginning of the loan.]]

formulaCard.formula: $$\text{Monthly Payment} = \frac{\text{Finance Charge} + \text{Amount Financed}}{\text{Number of Payments}}$$ $$\text{or}$$ $$\text{Monthly Payment} = \frac{\text{Amount Financed}}{100} \times \text{Amortization Factor}$$
notes: The amortization factor depends on APR and number of payments.
The formula method requires knowing the finance charge first.

explanation: Apply the blueprint to installment problems:
1. Understand: identify cash price, down payment, monthly payment, number of payments.
2. Solve: compute amount financed, total of payments, finance charge, lookup number (for APR table), and monthly payment.
3. Conclude: state the deferred payment price, APR range, and compare to cash price; advise on whether the credit is expensive.
This systematic approach ensures no step is missed.
